title: Monitoring of regional ventilation distribution during flexible bronchoscopy using electrical impedance tomography (FlexBrEIT)
summary:
Critically ill children in the intensive care unit often require mechanical ventilation via an endotracheal tube for prolonged periods. Children with severe respiratory failure represent a particularly high-risk group in this context.
During mechanical ventilation and for airway clearance, a bronchoscopic examination of the lungs is often necessary. This procedure is known as flexible tracheobronchoscopy (TB). TB is used to remove airway obstructions, clear secretions, and obtain mucus samples for testing, for example for viruses or bacteria. At the physician’s discretion, these procedures are performed during mechanical ventilation via an endotracheal tube. For this purpose, children are placed in an induced coma and receive muscle-relaxing medication to ensure the safe performance of the procedure.
Another group of children who frequently require bronchoscopic examinations includes those with congenital lung malformations and children following surgery of the trachea or lungs. These children are regularly scheduled for follow-up visits, during which the lungs are examined using bronchoscopy.
To date, it remains unclear how air distribution within the lungs is affected during TB. Until recently, there were no imaging methods in pediatric intensive care that allowed this to be assessed at the bedside, particularly without the use of ionizing radiation.
It is now possible to monitor lung ventilation distribution continuously at the bedside and without radiation using Electrical Impedance Tomography (EIT). EIT measurements are performed using a soft belt placed around the patient’s chest. Depending on the manufacturer, these belts are approved for use in preterm and newborn infants with a body weight of more than 0.5 kg. EIT is based on differences in electrical conductivity between body tissues, for example due to varying or changing gas content, as is the case in the lungs.
The measurement is performed via electrodes integrated into the belt. To date, only a limited number of studies have reported findings on air distribution during bronchoscopic procedures in children or adults.

interventions.name: As part of flexible tracheobronchoscopies (TB), which are performed electively in mechanically ventilated pediatric patients or in pediatric patients electively admitted to the intensive care unit, regional ventilation distribution and lung mechanics will be monitored using Electrical Impedance Tomo

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All patients requiring long-term invasive ventilation and needing flexible tracheostomy under sedation, or 2) short-term mechanical ventilation (sedation with a laryngeal mask) as part of a planned routine tracheostomy, are eligible for inclusion in the study.
Exclusion criteria:
1) Patients receiving palliative care     
2) Lack of parental consent    
3) Contraindications to performing the EIT measurement as per the approval (e.g., an implanted pacemaker) or the inability to perform the EIT measurement on the chest due to wound dressings or implanted drains.
